Requesting changes. Splitting long words into width-sized pieces looks right, but the PR also quietly tightens the rule for when a word fits on a line, and that's almost certainly a bug.

The fit check changed from `len(current) + 1 + len(chunk) <= width` to `< width`. Two words can now only share a line if the result is strictly shorter than `width`. For example, `wrap_text("ab cd", 5)` now returns `["ab", "cd"]` instead of `["ab cd"]`, even though `"ab cd"` is exactly 5 characters. Ordinary word wrapping, and presumably the "at most `width` characters" promise in the docstring, allows a line to be exactly `width` long. It's also inconsistent within the PR: a single word or split piece can be exactly `width` characters, but a line built from several words never can.

I don't have the test file, so I can't say for sure why this was changed. It looks like it was tweaked until one failing test passed, rather than fixing the actual cause, and the PR has no description to explain it.

Before this can merge:
1. Change the check back to `<=`, unless a test really does require lines shorter than `width`. If one does, the docstring needs to say so and the PR needs to explain why.
2. Run the full test suite and list the results in the PR description.
3. Minor: the new `if current:` check is never needed, because the early `return []` already covers empty input. It's harmless, though.
